quote: So my question around solar is gonna be not with that house.
stewart_read: This is a structurally non-standard lead — the customer doesn't own the home he wants solar info for, doesn't have a bill, doesn't have an address to qualify. The rep continues the standard verify flow briefly before adapting, but this is genuinely outside the scripted qualification path rather than a rep error.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep should have immediately abandoned the verify sequence and asked clarifying questions about the future home (timeline, location) instead of continuing to reference the current address.
coaching_implication: Flag this as a lead-type edge case for Kenny: no current qualifying address, no bill, speculative future purchase. Coach the rep on quickly identifying 'not this house' calls and re-routing to a short discovery instead of persisting on irrelevant verify items.

quote: So those they're we're, like, we have those on order, but they don't come out for, like, another couple years.
stewart_read: The customer's actual stated interest — solar shingles — is a product Ion doesn't currently offer per the schema (ion_does_NOT_sell.tesla_solar_roof_tiles), and the rep's answer is vague and uncertain rather than a clean redirect to what Ion does offer.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have been trying to stay honest rather than oversell, which is a reasonable instinct, but the response lacked a bridge to Ion's actual product (owned panels + Powerwall) that could have kept the customer engaged.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to have a ready, confident answer distinguishing what Ion sells now vs. future roadmap items, and to pivot to Ion's current offering rather than leaving the gap open-ended.

quote: May I ask you something? Are you paying a high power bill?
stewart_read: After the original address is disqualified, the rep pivots to the bill question as a strategic attempt to find a still-live angle on the current home before the conversation ends — this reads as a coherent recovery move, not a random reactive question.
alternative_hypothesis: A purely reactive read would say the rep just grabbed for any question to keep the call going, but the direct line from this question to the targeted bill-swap pitch at 02:08 shows intent.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this instinct — pivoting to the bill anchor when the original qualifying question dead-ends is the right move — while coaching the follow-through (see 02:20 miss).

quote: he he knows his stuff can get transferred. But sometimes that's a a hang up for for new people if they don't want that option
stewart_read: The customer surfaces a specific, credentialed objection (his realtor advised against a solar lien complicating a near-term sale) that maps directly to the objection_inversion pattern — the same bill pain justifying solar is being used as a reason not to act. The rep does not flip this; instead moves to a logistics question about installation cost.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this objection as unresolvable given the stated 3-year sale timeline, making a flip low-value here — but the schema's inversion move exists precisely for this kind of resistance and was never attempted.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep on at least attempting one inversion or clarifying question here (e.g., asking what savings the bill swap would generate before the sale) rather than moving straight to a yes/no installation-cost check.

quote: You said, like, two one to two years for for that. Is that just your company, or is that other companies out there?
stewart_read: The customer references having submitted a form that was 'supposed to look at all all the different solar companies,' implying he may be in a multi-company lead funnel. The rep does not probe this for competitive intel.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the call is already closing, probing here may have been low-yield — the customer is disengaging, not comparison-shopping actively.
coaching_implication: Minor coaching note: even a 10-second question here ('did any other companies reach out to you on this form?') would have given the closer/next contact useful context, at near-zero cost to the wrap-up.

quote: I think probably right now, I'm just gonna I'm gonna up the brakes a little bit that and so they go forward.
stewart_read: The call ends with a polite decline and no next step — no callback date, no offer to follow up when the customer is closer to purchasing the new home, no text confirmation of any kind.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer explicitly disqualified himself (no current home, 3-year timeline, informational-only intent), a no_appointment outcome may be the correct and only available result — this is not purely a procedural miss.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close speculative/future-intent leads with a light-touch future callback ('makes sense — when you're closer to the move, want me to check back in with you?') instead of a bare goodbye, to keep the lead warm for recycling.
